critical_issues.msg: Plan creates models for five tables (tenants, users, roles, permissions, user_roles) that already exist under the same names in src/db/models/ — both files subclass a Base, and SQLAlchemy requires one Base per table. Registering the same table name under a different Base causes mapper conflicts at runtime.
critical_issues.suggestion: Either make the internal/ models inherit from db.base.Base (consolidating into src/db/models/) or give the identity tables different __tablename__ values (e.g. 'identity_tenants') to avoid the registry collision. Align the plan with whichever path is intended.

critical_issues.msg: Five models (TenantModel, UserModel, RoleModel, PermissionModel, UserRoleModel) use __tablename__ values that are already registered to Base from db.base (in src/db/models/tenant.py, user.py, rbac.py). SQLAlchemy declarative bases are independent registries — assigning the same table name to a different Base subclass produces undefined mapper behavior and will fail or silently corrupt queries.
critical_issues.suggestion: Have identity.py import and extend from db.base.Base instead of internal.db.engine.Base, or move these 5 models into src/db/models/ and keep only OrganizationModel/DepartmentModel in internal/. Alternatively, rename the tables (e.g. __tablename__ = 'id_tenants') with migration support.

suggestions.msg: Clean re-export of all 8 identity model classes — no standalone issues, but it inherits the identity.py conflict.

Rule 22 / PEP 8 violation: mapped_column(JSON, default=dict) uses a mutable default argument (the dict literal). The same dict object is shared across all instances until the column replaces it at INSERT time.
suggestions.suggestion: Use default=lambda: dict or default=dict (callable) so the callable is invoked per-row: mapped_column(JSON, default=lambda: dict, nullable=False)

suggestions.msg: DepartmentModel.children relationship uses cascade='all, delete-orphan' on a self-referential FK with parent_id. Without an index on parent_id, hierarchical queries (children loader) at scale can degrade.
suggestions.suggestion: Add index=True to the parent_id mapped_column: mapped_column(ForeignKey('departments.id', ondelete='SET NULL'), nullable=True, index=True)

suggestions.msg: Rule 4 (classes represent real domain concepts) / Rule 11 (meaningful names): The guard 'not hasattr(TenantModel, "__table__")' is dead code — SQLAlchemy declarative classes always have __table__. The left side of 'or' always evaluates True so the right side always runs; however the test still passes because the second branch is correct. Keeping the dead branch is misleading.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the hasattr guard and keep only: assert 'tenant_id' not in [c.name for c in TenantModel.__table__.columns]
